provenance.statement: Let users export their invoices as CSV. It must reuse the existing Report Builder and finish in under 10 seconds for 10,000 rows.

assumptions: The export is a user-initiated action on invoice data the user is already permitted to see.
"Under 10 seconds for 10,000 rows" is measured end to end from the export request to the CSV being available to the user.
Report Builder is an existing component in this system that can be extended or called to produce the export.

ambiguities.question: Which users can export invoices: all users, or only certain roles? And does each user export only their own invoices or also others' invoices they can view?
Which invoices and which fields are included in the CSV (all invoices, a filtered or selected subset, a date range; which columns)?

What does 'reuse the existing Report Builder' require concretely: must the export go through Report Builder's public interface, or may it be extended or modified, and what if Report Builder cannot produce CSV today?
What are the performance measurement conditions (hardware, concurrent load, percentile such as p95 or worst case, cold or warm start) for the 10-second limit?
What is the expected behavior above 10,000 rows (also under 10 seconds, degrade gracefully, asynchronous export, row cap)?
How is the CSV delivered to the user (browser download, email, stored file) and where is the export triggered in the UI or API?
Are there CSV format requirements (delimiter, encoding, header row, date and currency formatting, escaping of special characters)?

acceptance_criteria.statement: A user can export their invoices as a CSV file.
The invoice CSV export reuses the existing Report Builder rather than introducing a separate export implementation.
Exporting 10,000 invoice rows to CSV completes in under 10 seconds.
